workflow.critical: The workflow execution engine is governed by: {project-root}/_bmad/core/tasks/workflow.xml
You MUST have already loaded and processed: {installed_path}/workflow.yaml
⚠️ ABSOLUTELY NO TIME ESTIMATES. Do NOT mention hours, days, weeks, or timelines.

🧠 AUTONOMOUS DECISION PROTOCOL — ACTIVE FOR ENTIRE LOOP EXECUTION
When autonomous_mode == true (set during initialization):
1. ALL <ask> tags in ANY sub-workflow (dev-story, code-review, create-story, retrospective) MUST be AUTO-ANSWERED by YOU using your best judgment. DO NOT wait for user input. Simply log your decision briefly and continue.
2. DECISION INTELLIGENCE RULES — when auto-answering, follow these priorities:
CODE-REVIEW decisions: - "Fix them automatically" → ALWAYS choose this. Fix all HIGH and MEDIUM issues. - Never choose "create action items" or "show details" — just fix and move on.
DEV-STORY decisions: - Story discovery → The loop already provides story_path. Use it directly. - "No stories found" options → Skip, the loop handles routing. - HALT: 3 consecutive failures → Log the failure, skip story, continue loop. - HALT: dependencies needed → Install/add if safe, otherwise skip story. - HALT: config missing → Log and skip story, continue loop. - Ambiguous task requirements → Use best judgment based on AC and Dev Notes.
CREATE-STORY decisions: - Story selection → The loop provides story_key. Use it directly. - "No sprint-status" → Never happens (loop verifies first). - "No backlog stories" → Return to loop, it will route elsewhere. - Any template-output checkpoints → Auto-continue (#yolo style).
RETROSPECTIVE decisions: - Epic selection → The loop provides epic_num. Use it directly. - Party-mode discussions → Run in #yolo mode: simulate agent discussion concisely, extract key lessons, generate retrospective document. Do NOT run interactive dialogue. - Action items → Generate SMART action items autonomously. - "Epic update required" → Log the flag, continue loop. User reviews after loop completes.
GENERAL RULES: - template-output checkpoints → Always auto-continue (never prompt [a/c/p/y]). - "Continue to next step?" prompts → Always yes. - Any "exit/quit" option → NEVER choose. Always continue. - When in doubt → Choose the option that KEEPS THE LOOP MOVING.
3. LOGGING: For every auto-decision, output ONE line: `⚡ AUTO: [workflow] [decision made] — [brief reason]` Then immediately continue execution. No pausing.
4. HALT ESCALATION: The ONLY things that stop the loop are: - max_iterations reached - ALL stories are done (sprint complete) - A sub-workflow fails 3 times on the SAME story (skip it, continue others) - User explicitly presses Ctrl+C

🔀 MODEL SWITCHING PROTOCOL
When model_strategy == "optimized" (from workflow.yaml):
Each sub-workflow SHOULD be executed on the model specified in {model_map}. The orchestrator uses the Task tool with the `model` parameter to spawn sub-workflows on the appropriate model.
MODEL ASSIGNMENTS (from workflow.yaml model_map): - create-story → opus (heavy context analysis, cross-referencing architecture) - dev-story → sonnet (code implementation, TDD, fast iteration) - code-review → opus (adversarial review, deep reasoning) - retrospective → opus (synthesis, pattern detection, strategic analysis) - routing → haiku (sprint-status parsing, simple decisions)
IMPLEMENTATION: When invoking a sub-workflow, use the Task tool like this: Task(subagent_type="general-purpose", model="{model_map.workflow_name}", prompt="...")
The prompt MUST include: 1. Load workflow.xml engine: @_bmad/core/tasks/workflow.xml 2. Execute specific workflow: @_bmad/bmm/workflows/4-implementation/{workflow}/workflow.yaml 3. The autonomous_mode flag and decision protocol 4. All relevant parameters (story_path, story_key, epic_num)
When model_strategy == "single": - Do NOT use the Task tool for model switching - Use invoke-workflow directly (all workflows run on session model) - This is the fallback for users who prefer a single model
LOGGING: When switching models, output: `🔀 MODEL: {{workflow}} → {{model}} ({{reason}})`
